title: TermAl source capture and committed-input admission treat a deep Windows worktree of a real consumer (Phoenix/Questly) as dirty or unmeasured because child paths exceed MAX_PATH
outcome: On Windows, a clean git worktree of PhoenixCodeNav or Questly placed under a Git-ignored 'target' path (as TermAl's watcher requires) can be measured by TermAl's host source capture and admitted by the committed-input lane even when child paths exceed MAX_PATH. If that is not possible, it is refused with a reason that names the long-path cause and the remedy. It is never reported as a generic dirty child or a silent 'unmeasured'.
acceptance: On Windows, the EXISTING rev-5 committed-source measurement (committed_source_status / committed_source_submodules in src/ordinary_commit_input.rs, used by the committed-input lane and the native route) measures a clean worktree whose child paths exceed MAX_PATH, such as a Phoenix worktree under artifacts/target/b, as clean at its commit. It needs no per-repository, global or system core.longpaths setting: core.longpaths=true is supplied for those Git invocations only, and it reaches submodule processes too. A dirty file in such a child is still reported dirty.
If a long path still cannot be read, the measurement refuses with a reason naming the long-path cause and the remedy; it is never a generic dirty child or a silent 'unmeasured'.

Windows regression tests cover a clean fixture child with paths over 260 characters and a dirty one. Behaviour off Windows and the rev-5 predicate are otherwise unchanged. No new source_id, reader or predicate is added.

On Windows, the existing rev-5 committed-source measurement never reports a worktree as clean when Git could not fully read a child path, whether it fails, exits 0 with an error on stderr, or reports a long-path error. Such a reading is refused with a named long-path reason; a tracked change in a long-path child is reported NotClean or refused, never Taken. A regression test covers the dirty long-path child without core.longpaths, reproducing the false-clean of test-3c7e3e97 before the fix and refusing or reporting NotClean after it.

completion.summary: Git reads through ReviewFreezeGit now refuse incomplete output instead of reporting a false clean, and Windows long paths in deep consumer worktrees (Phoenix, Questly) are measured, so committed-input admission and source capture no longer treat them as dirty or unmeasured.
